# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart that the doctors have been monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, which makes meal times very stressful, and he's extremely picky and refuses many foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets exhausted very quickly when playing outside or running around, and he has speech difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) or ADHD.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks people to repeat what they've said because he didn't catch it the first time, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things that are far away, like the board in his classroom.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth seem to break or chip really easily, even with proper care.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth or other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties may affect his learning, and he may require extra support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech difficulties and may have behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the patient's hearing and address any potential hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor the patient's vision and address any potential vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and address any potential concerns.
* Speech therapy to address the patient's speech difficulties.
* Behavioral therapy to address any potential behavioral differences.
* Occupational therapy to support the patient's development and address any potential delays.
* Physiotherapy to support the patient's physical development and address any potential delays.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing during active play, which is a concern for the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than normal during active play, raising concerns about potential heart issues. However, the pediatrician has not seemed too concerned yet.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is managed with diet and occasional medication under the doctor's guidance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient tires easily when running around or playing actively and has speech delay, for which she is working with a speech therapist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and many have developmental delay and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear once, which took a while to clear up, and her hearing is monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means her eyeballs are slightly larger than usual, and this has been noticeable since birth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth, and her parents are taking good care of them through regular brushing and dental visits.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel and require regular dental check-ups, and some have other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is working with a speech therapist to address her speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and tires easily, which may be related to developmental delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, and many have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and prevent further issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to ensure the patient's hearing is not affected by the previous ear fluid issue.
* Ophthalmology review to monitor the patient's hypermetropia and prevent any further vision problems.
* Speech therapy to address the patient's speech delay.
* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and referral for endocrine investigations if necessary.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and behavioral therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioral concerns.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing concerns, with inconsistent responses to sounds, and may have difficulty hearing certain frequencies.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was slower to do things like walking and sitting when he was little and took longer than other kids to learn them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes doesn't respond when called, and may have hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes a lot when trying to focus, which may indicate a vision problem.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, and he needs to be careful about what he eats.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with short fingers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to detect any potential hearing difficulties
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for any skeletal abnormalities
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and behavioural differences
